steps.path: The first screen after installing: 'getting things ready' (before = today's app)
steps.headline: Side-by-side logo, bigger, with the tagline tucked beside the 'y' as approved; Outfit for every word; a thicker bar.
steps.changed: The logo uses your approved side-by-side spacing (round 26) at an 80px icon. All setup text is in Outfit now (your Q-2), the heading is larger, and the bar is thicker with a faint glow in the name's colours.
steps.notice: The first thing a new user sees looks like the brand boards, not like a settings page.
steps.risk: The tool names are gone, as you picked last round; on a Mac the line instead says to click Install in Apple's window.

steps.path: When a step fails (before = last round)
steps.headline: A failure is one white card: a soft stop sign, 'Setup stopped', one sentence, a gradient Retry button and 'Show details'.
steps.changed: The grey error strip and separate 'Show details' box became a single card. Retry is the screen's one filled button, in the name's purple-to-pink. 'Show details' is a quiet link that opens the full message inside the card.
steps.notice: It reads as a calm pause with one obvious next step, not as an error dump.
steps.risk: The card isn't the app's standard error strip; it is setup's own, like the rest of the brand surface.

variants.label: A · All three open
variants.summary: Three white cards, each with a badge (No extra cost / Pay per message / Private), three facts with small icons, and white buttons led by the Claude, ChatGPT and OpenRouter logos.
variants.risk: Tall: the third card and the backup warning need a scroll on a laptop screen.

variants.label: B · Pick a kind first
variants.summary: Three rows with the companies' logos, a badge and an arrow; clicking one opens its facts and logo buttons (right half shows 'Pay as you go' opened), with '‹ All options' to go back.
variants.risk: One extra click, and the facts can't be compared side by side.

steps.path: After pressing a sign-in button, while the browser is open
steps.headline: The 'finish signing in your browser' wait now has a Cancel button (from master) and sits in the same white card.
steps.changed: Master added Cancel on this screen while we were working; it's carried into the new look.
steps.notice: Changing your mind after pressing a sign-in button no longer means restarting the app.

steps.path: The 'Start your first session' screen right after setup
steps.headline: The 'Start your first session' screen gets its own round once setup is approved, built to match it.
steps.changed: Stated, not asked: you rejected all four versions last round. Rather than guess again in parallel, I'll design it from the approved setup look so the hand-off from setup into the app feels continuous.
steps.notice: Next deck after this one is that screen alone.

steps.path: How setup gets Node.js and Git
steps.headline: Your bundling question is already answered on master: setup downloads its own Git and Node.js, without winget.
steps.changed: Stated: while we worked, master shipped exactly the option you picked: Git comes from the official ready-to-run download into YouCoded's own folder (no winget, no admin prompt), and Node.js installs only when someone chooses Claude Code. Master also removed the Windows Developer Mode step. I merged master into this branch, so the screens here use it.
steps.notice: The failure on your Windows machine can't happen that way any more; this branch is now up to date with master.
